tra_loi.vat: Tricorne (cocked) hats worn with matching red livery coats by the men on a state barge
tra_loi.dac_diem: The men on the barge wear black hats with the brim folded up into three corners and edged with trim. Several wear them: the standing figure at right, the men under the canopy, and the rowers. The rowers wear uniform red coats with white cuffs. The central man has a long curled wig and a dark coat with a white cravat. The barge has a gilded canopy with red drapes.
tra_loi.ly_do: The tricorne became common in the 1680s–1690s, and the matching red coats with cuffs look like early 18th-century livery. In 1666 men wore broad-brimmed hats with plumes or loosely turned brims, and the crisp three-cornered shape was not yet standard.

ghi_chu.mo_ta: The royal barge has a gilded canopy with red velvet drapes and swag curtains. The hull is heavily carved and gilded, with a curved prow. The rowers sit on benches and pull long oars.
ghi_chu.ly_do: This looks like a Georgian or Baroque state barge in the style of the 1732 Prince's barge. A Thames royal barge of 1666 would have been plainer.

ghi_chu.mo_ta: The man in the foreground wears a light-coloured long wig and a long buff coat. The other man wears a full dark curly wig with a white jabot.
ghi_chu.ly_do: Long full-bottomed wigs were in fashion by the 1670s and later. The long frock-style coat is also a later style, though some of this dress is close to 1666 fashion.
